steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Lightly grease two 8x4 inch loaf pans.
Combine cream cheese, 1/2 cup sugar, 1 tablespoon flour, 1 egg and orange zest in a medium bowl; beat until smooth. Set aside.
Sift together 1 ⅔ cups flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, cloves, and pumpkin pie spice; set aside.
Place pumpkin, vegetable oil, 2 eggs and 1 ½ cups sugar in a large bowl; beat well. Stir the pumpkin mixture into the flour mixture just until combined. Fold in the pecans if desired.
Pour 1/2 of the pumpkin batter into the loaf pans. Spoon cream cheese mixture on top of this layer and then pour on the remaining batter.
Bake in preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into center of the loaf comes out clean, about 60 to 70 minutes. Cool bread in pans briefly before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Cream Cheese Bread
raw_recipe.description: This pumpkin bread has a layer of sweetened cream cheese with orange zest that pairs perfectly with the spices in the loaf for a delicious fall treat.

video.description: This pumpkin bread makes for the perfect fall treat! In this video, Natalie shows you how to make this chocolate chip pumpkin bread recipe that incorporates chocolate chips and a creamy, flavorful cream cheese filling into a classic pumpkin bread loaf. Split your pumpkin batter in half, spoon in the cream cheese filling in the middle, and bake until set and ready to slice.

review.reviewBody: Oh my gosh! This is the absolute best bread!! The only thing I did was to omit the orange peel and used 1/4tsp. van. extract instead and left out cloves and increased cinnamon to 1 tsp. It came out delish, I'm tossing out all my other recipes I have for pumpkin bread! As another veiwer stated be careful not to put too much in 1st layer or cheese ends up to close to the top. I'm going to make 2 more loaves right now for Thanksgiving because we can't stop eating the ones I just made!! Thanks Tina!!!

My family ate all the bread within 2 days. This is an excellent recipe. I also omitted the orange peel and substituted vanilla in the cheese filling. On the bread mixture I left out the gloves and doubled up on cinnamon. It was delicious and worked out well for me because I didn't have orange zest or cloves on hand. I also didn't have 2 bread pans, so I used the second half to make cupcakes. They cooked a lot faster than the bread and my family thought they were the best cupcakes they had ever had. They reminded me of the seasonal ones you can get at Starbucks, but at a fraction of the cost. Thanks Tina for sharing this recipe with us.

I’ve made this twice. Both times, I had to substitute the orange peel for 1tbsp citrus concentrate (sea buckthorn) because I didn’t have orange and need to use up the sea buckthorn. I have made it both as a loaf and as muffins, since I have only one loaf pan. Both are amazing but muffins are easier for sharing with neighbours and sending home with guests. The loaf stayed super moist! I made anywhere from 3 to six muffins plus the loaf, depending on how much I wanted of each. The muffins took about 1/2 hr to bake. I also once substituted 1/2tsp extra cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ginger, and 1/4 tsp nutmeg for the pumpkin pie spice since I didn’t have any. It was amazing both ways.

This was so good! I saw another reviewer had increased the pumpkin and eggs to make a 9x5 loaves. I did the same thing only increasing all the cake ingredients to make 3 - 8 x 4 loafs because I happened to have three of the disposable one. I increased the pumpkin to a whole can, 3 eggs, 2 cups flour and increased the spices to 3/4 tsp each. So, so good! This will be a recipe to go into my cookbook of favorites.

This bread was good but I thought it needed more spice. I didn't have any orange zest, so added 1/4tsp. vanilla as the other reviewer suggested and omit the cloves and up the cinnamon to 1tsp. I also didn't have 2 loaf pan, so I use 8x8 inch pan and worked out perfect. It took 70 mins. to cook. If I were to make these again, I'm gonna add a bit more spice and maybe throw in some walnuts or pecans.

I have been making pumpkin breads w/ and w/out cream cheese for a long time, but this is by far the best recipe I have ever tried. I only had large loaf pans, so I used the whole recipe in one pan and increased the oven temp to 350 degrees and increased the time to 1 hour, 30 minutes. Turned out great!

Delicious! I substituted half applesauce for half the vegetable oil. Next time I will try substituting applesauce for all the oil. Liked the orange flavor in the cream cheese. I didn’t have an orange to zest, so I used orange extract.

Loved It! I actually made one bread and doubled the layers - Pumpkin batter; cream cheese filling; pumpkin batter; cream cheese and then the rest of the batter! I love the cream cheese filling, I actually used 12 oz. of cream cheese. Used vanilla (as suggested by reviewers) in place of orange zest - glad I did. Took a bit longer to cook (I have a small oven so as far as time to cook, I just kept checking on it every 15 mins. after an hr. of cooking which is probably why mine sunk in the middle). Will definitely make it again!

Note: To GramChase - I had to spoon mine into the pan as you.

The cream cheese part of this bread is SUPER! The bread part was a little bland for my taste. I will make it again though, and probably increase the spices. My minor alterations: I didn't have two pans handy, so I cooked it all in one 8x8 pan. I used 1 tablespoon of vanilla instead of orange zest (because of preference). I baked it at 350 in the 8x8 and it took 1h and 5 min.

This is EXCELLENT! I cut the recipe in half and was positive I messed it up because the “top layer” of bread mix didn’t really cover all of the cream cheese layer and the cream cheese filling seemed to rise before the bread, but it all worked out and was amazing. I added about a quarter teaspoon of vanilla to the cream cheese filling and used a hand mixer to fluff it up a bit.
This is a fantastic pumpkin bread. I adapted the recipe to make 1.5 of the original recipe (my loaves were a little short). Put the filling in a piping bag for easy and even layers.
I was unable to travel with a pie on the bus so found this Thanksgiving gem. Everyone was impressed and some liked it more than pie! The orange with the cream cheese is so subtle, it's perfect
I didn't realize it makes two loaves and poured it all into one pan 😑 but it tastes delicious
Didn't work out for me. It burnt.

I loved it. My 14 yr old daughter only liked the cream cheese filling. I did add pecans and instead of white sugar, I used Splenda. I also did not have the orange zest. I liked that it wasn't sweet sweet. The bread and cream cheese filling gave it just the amount of sweet that I was hoping for
I’ve literally made this three times in the last 7 days for 2 Friendsgivings and thanksgiving and it was a hit every single time!
great
I onlt tried this recipe because of the cream cheese filling. Overall it was way too sweet and the pumpkin bread part was not a true bread texture. I will not be trying this one again.
This bread is absolutely delicious. I followed the recipe as is and would not change a thing. The orange zest is the perfect touch.

This pumpkin bread is soooo unbelievably good! The orange cheesecake filling complements the spicy pumpkin flavor so well. The breads are super moist, and incredibly flavorful. I didn't change a thing about the recipe and the loaves were perfectly baked in 70 minutes. My loaves were a little on the squat side, but that doesn't bother me. They still look nice--but more importantly, they taste amazing!! Thank you for sharing your recipe!
